questions.title: Which circuit will Formula One announce as the replacement venue for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix?
questions.background: The Bahrain Grand Prix originally scheduled for April 2026 was cancelled amid conflict in the Middle East.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Formula One's first official announcement after May 1, 2026 identifying a replacement host circuit for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix. Resolution Conditions : The announcement must occur by December 31, 2026. Resolution is based on the announced venue, regardless of whether the race is subsequently held or receives final regulatory approval. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the circuit.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-18 major refresh (first since June 24, incorporating Crash.net July 5 and F1Oversteer/Nextgen Auto July 15): F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali stated on July 5 that F1 aims to fill the vacant Oct 4 slot (between Baku and Singapore) with a decision required before the summer break following the July 26 Hungarian GP. With Middle East conflict continuing (July 17 IRGC al-Tanf strike claim and ongoing Strait of Hormuz closure) clouding any return to the Gulf, F1 chiefs are evaluating European/regional replacements. New July 15 reporting significantly reshuffles candidate odds: (1) Istanbul Park formally offered to step in ahead of its 2027 deal and fits the Baku-to-Singapore Oct 4 geography best, but faces rushed renovation/homologation hurdles and lower crowd projections, trimming it from 0.40 -> 0.30; (2) Algarve International Circuit (Portimao) was explicitly highlighted in both July 5 Crash.net and July 15 F1Oversteer reports as ready to step in ahead of its 2027 deal with a valid Grade 1 licence, lifting it sharply from 0.15 -> 0.23; (3) Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari (Imola) remains a prime turnkey Grade 1 option named July 15 (0.21 -> 0.19); (4) Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya enters at 0.10 after circuit chiefs formally offered a second 2026 race and July 15 reporting named Barcelona alongside Imola and Portimao as the most likely option if teams block FOM's preferred double-header; (5) Baku City Circuit enters at 0.04 (replacing unmentioned Sepang/Paul Ricard) as FOM's preferred double-header option adjacent to Oct 4 despite current team opposition. Top-5 sum = 0.86, leaving 0.14 for Sepang, Mugello, Paul Ricard, Singapore/Las Vegas double-headers, or other Grade 1 tracks.

local_articles.title: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos in talks to join consortium seeking 30% stake in Liverpool
local_articles.snippet: The Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has held talks about joining the consortium that is seeking to buy around 30 per cent of Liverpool. The group led by the former Queens Park Rangers co‑owner Amit Bhatia has made a provisional offer of £1.35bn (€1.58bn) to buy a stake from Fenway Sports Group (FSG), and is talking to other potential investors over supplying funding. Bezos has a personal fortune of around $257bn (€301bn), according to Forbes, making him the fourth-richest person in the world. The 62-year-old has previously explored bids for the NFL franchises Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders without completing a deal, but has never before looked at investing in the Premier League. Sources with knowledge of the talks have indicated that any deal with Bhatia’s consortium would see Bezos receive equity in Liverpool. local_articles.title: Spain keeper Rodriguez joins Arsenal after six years at Real
local_articles.snippet: July 22 - Spain goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez, who captained Real Madrid last season, has joined Arsenal on a free transfer after six years at the Spanish club, the Women's Super League side said on Wednesday. • Rodriguez has represented Spain 24 times, and was part of the squad when they won the Women's World Cup in 2023 and the Women's Nations League the following year. • The 27-year-old has made 215 appearances for Real over six seasons. • "I’m really excited to be part of the team and take on this new challenge. I want to help us compete for trophies," said Rodriguez. • Arsenal, who finished second behind Manchester City last season, begin their WSL campaign when the league kicks off in September. REUTERS

questions.title: Who will be appointed Peru's foreign minister in the incoming presidential administration's first cabinet in July 2026?
questions.background: A new presidential administration is scheduled to take office in Peru in July 2026. Its foreign minister will oversee the country's diplomatic relations.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Peruvian government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the person officially appointed minister of foreign affairs in the incoming administration's first cabinet, with the appointment announced by July 31, 2026. Speculation about potential appointments does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed foreign minister's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-13 to 2026-07-15 Peruvian transition breakthrough across El Comercio, Infobae, Gestion, and Gato Encerrado: former 2026 presidential candidate and Sí Creo party leader Carlos Espá has emerged as the clear frontrunner to become Keiko Fujimori's Foreign Minister. Crucially, El Comercio (July 14) reveals that Carla Mares Ruiz—previously accredited to Fujimori's Foreign Ministry transition team (ETTE) at Torre Tagle—was Sí Creo's Senate candidate alongside her former Universidad del Pacífico student president Giacomo Sanguinetti Ravettino, providing strong structural evidence that Torre Tagle is being lined up for Espá. Espá met privately with Fujimori and expected incoming Premier Luis Galarreta on July 13, declined to deny Canciller reports ('hay que tener paciencia'; 'dispuestos a poner nuestro granito de arena'), and Gato Encerrado (July 15) cited a Fujimorismo insider explicitly naming Carlos Espá as incoming Foreign Minister on the same day Fujimori received her JNE credentials and announced a multipartisan ('multipartidario') first cabinet. Promoting Carlos Espá directly to #1 at a disciplined 0.45 (respecting the unconfirmed-appointment cap given potential vetting/diplomatic pushback before July 27-28), trimming career/former-FM fallbacks Javier González-Olaechea (0.12 -> 0.08), Hugo de Zela (0.11 -> 0.08), Elmer Schialer (0.07 -> 0.05), and Carlos Pareja (0.06 -> 0.04), dropping Alfredo Ferrero, and keeping 30% residual for Torre Tagle's diplomatic bench or another multipartisan appointee.

questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-17 update: frontrunner Andy Flower publicly and formally ruled himself out of the England Test head coach race at London Spirit's media day (BBC Sport, Sky Sports, Reuters, ESPNcricinfo, Hindustan Times), confirming he turned down the ECB even with dual-role IPL flexibility because IPL/RCB duties clash with the early English summer. Following Flower's withdrawal, iNews Cricket Correspondent Chris Stocks reports on July 17 that the ECB is now pivoting to former Australia coach Justin Langer as its top target (rated 4/5; strong Ashes rebuilding pedigree and county familiarity, though tempered by LSG IPL ties and past intensity concerns), lifting Langer 0.13 -> 0.26. Newly available Stephen Fleming (co-rated 4/5 by iNews, named by BBC Sport July 17) rises 0.19 -> 0.25 as he just left CSK after 18 years—removing the IPL clash that deterred Flower—was Rob Key's 2022 preference, and publicly welcomed an approach this week. Among remaining shortlisted contenders, Jonathan Trott (0.15 -> 0.16, English, available, named by BBC Sport/iNews 3/5), Richard Dawson (0.07 -> 0.09, English, ECB pathway, named by BBC Sport July 17), and Tom Moody (new entry at 0.07, explicitly named by BBC Sport July 17 alongside Trott, Dawson, and Fleming) round out the top 5, leaving 17% residual for Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, and unlisted options as BBC notes the ECB is still in an initial stage and open to an interim for August's Pakistan series.

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will announce a finalized voluntary repatriation plan for thousands of Myanmar refugees in August 2026?
questions.background: Repatriation means returning refugees to their country of origin. This question concerns finalization of a government plan, rather than the completion of refugee returns.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or reliable news reporting directly quoting those statements. Resolving Event : During August 2026, a Southeast Asian government publicly confirms that it has finalized a voluntary repatriation programme, or the first phase of such a programme, covering at least 1,000 refugees from Myanmar. A preliminary agreement to consider returns is insufficient. Actual departures need not have occurred. Accepted Answer Format : The common English name of the country finalizing the repatriation plan, not the destination country.
questions.current_reasoning: Only Southeast Asian countries qualify (excluding Bangladesh), and Thailand and Malaysia host over 95% of Myanmar refugees in Southeast Asia. Thailand hosts 80,155 registered camp refugees, is actively implementing a border camp-closure timeline announced in May-June 2026, has prior UNHCR voluntary-return precedent, and enjoys the closest ties with Min Aung Hlaing's April 2026 administration. Malaysia hosts ~190,000 UNHCR-registered Myanmar refugees (mostly Rohingya) and on June 22, 2026 PM Anwar Ibrahim and Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman explicitly vowed direct engagement with Myanmar authorities on repatriation, making Malaysia a close second, with Indonesia (~2,000-3,000 Rohingya) a distant third.

Meanwhile PlanetFootball (July 8) and Standard (July 14) note Man City (holding Rodri/Kovacic/Anderson) and Man Utd (cold trail, pursuing Tielemans) are not actively bidding. Promoting Arsenal sharply from 0.19 -> 0.55—capped at 0.55 under our unconfirmed-transfer discipline because Newcastle still demand £100m/€120m (a valuation gap that let Spurs hijack Tonali from Arsenal)—with Real Madrid (0.11), Manchester City (0.10, down from 0.24), Barcelona (0.06, cited by TEAMtalk as monitoring), and PSG (0.05) capturing hijack risk alongside 13% residual.
